method.summary: Fills low ground: each cell's height above the nearest mapped waterway, lagoon or sea (HAND, straight-line nearest), plus local depression filling from a priority-flood pass. Excess rain stands where it is deeper than the cell's HAND, and every hollow fills with the rain on itself and on the ground that drains into it, up to its rim; whichever is deeper wins.
method.dem: FABDEM 30 m (bare earth). GLO-30 was not used: it includes buildings.
method.smoothing: 5x5 mean filter (~150 m) before HAND and the fill, so DEM noise does not read as ponds.
method.hand: Euclidean nearest drainage cell, not routed along a flow path.
method.depressions: Priority-flood fill seeded at the window border and at every mapped water cell; each hollow then fills with the rain on itself and on its D8 catchment, capped by its rim.
method.limits: No drain network, no channel conveyance, no infiltration beyond the stated drain capacity: only height above water, hollows and catchment area.
method.stipple: Every other 30 m cell in the PNGs is drawn ~25% lighter, so the layer can never pass for a real flood.

crop.note: Cropped to the Lagos urban core (about 2.9-4.2 E). The Badagry and Epe outskirts are outside the model.

parameters.excess_rain: rain minus what the drains take away
parameters.storm_note: Drains sized at 10 mm/h take away 60 mm over a 6 h storm, so the 40 mm scenario is roughly a 100 mm storm.
parameters.max_depth_note: No cell is claimed deeper than 2 m: the DEM's vertical error is about 2 m.
parameters.built_up: GHSL 2020 built-up share >= 0.05 per cell; only these cells are modelled

terrain_verdict.summary: Our own test found 30 m terrain only weakly predicts which spot floods: flooded spots are about 2 cm lower than their surroundings while the DEM's vertical error is about 2 m.
lines: task 24b terrain check (fairer controls) - verdict: pass (decided by the 'local' design on FABDEM)
per-design verdicts (rule fixed before results; meta.verdict_rule in events/terrain_check.json):
builtup_only   FABDEM: mixed - 1/4 primary metrics significant after Holm in the all-points subset, 2/4 in the >2 km subset [all: tpi_min; >2 km: acc_log10_max, tpi_min]
builtup_only   GLO-30: fail - 0/4 primary metrics significant after Holm in the all-points subset, 1/4 in the >2 km subset
matched_water  FABDEM: mixed - 1/4 primary metrics significant after Holm in the all-points subset, 2/4 in the >2 km subset [all: tpi_min; >2 km: acc_log10_max, tpi_min]
matched_water  GLO-30: fail - 0/4 primary metrics significant after Holm in the all-points subset, 1/4 in the >2 km subset

validation.note: 0 of 178 spots sit outside the cropped window. A spot 'hits' when its own 30 m cell is model-wet. The random baseline is the share of built-up cells that are wet: scattering the spots at random would hit at that rate.

rendered.source: OpenFreeMap planet vector tiles (OpenMapTiles schema); buildings exist only in z14 tiles
rendered.note: Even where mapping is dense, a z14 tile carries only a few dozen building features, so the 3D view shows a sample of the buildings, not every one.

osm_underneath.source: OpenStreetMap building footprints (Geofabrik extract, way centres)
osm_underneath.note: OSM building coverage in Lagos is patchy; counts are real footprints, zeros included.

building_coverage.note: The 3D view shows buildings only where OSM has outlines, thinned further by the z14 tiles.
